articles.title: Schools banned a record 12,000 books in a year, according to annual report
articles.summary: Themes of race, sexuality and gender remain common reasons to ban books, as some school administrators use AI to determine what gets pulled, a new report finds.
articles.body: Nearly 12,000 bans took place in public schools over the past year, according to a new study from PEN America, the highest total since the free expression organization began tracking removals five years ago. For the second straight year, Stephen King was the author most likely to have his work withdrawn. Many of the bans took place in Florida and Texas, where restrictive laws have been passed and both politicians and conservative activists have pushed for removals. PEN has also found that school district administrators rely increasingly on AI to determine which books should be pulled. Themes of race, racism, sexuality and gender identity remain the most common reasons books are challenged. “School libraries make knowledge and ideas available, ensure books remain available for all regardless of personal or political ideologies, and open gateways to stories that inform, challenge, and reflect the realities of the world back to readers,” the PEN report, titled “Banned in the USA,” reads in part. “Book bans impede the freedom to read, cutting students’ access to a diversity of views, voices, perspectives, and literature they deserve to encounter.” In all, PEN found 11,982 cases of bans, affecting 7,370 individual works. Over 4,500 were on the list for the first time, ranging from the 19th century classic “Jane Eyre” to Sui Ishida’s “Tokyo Ghoul” manga series. Monday’s report arrives during Banned Books Week, when events at schools and libraries and other locations nationwide call attention to censorship efforts. King’s books were pulled 312 times, with “The Shining” and “The Green Mile” among those affected. Meanwhile, the most banned individual title was Patricia McCormick’s novel about a girl sold into sexual slavery in India, “Sold,” for which PEN found 25 removals. Other books commonly targeted include Margaret Atwood’s dystopian “The Handmaid’s Tale”; Laurie Halse Anderson’s “Speak,” her prize-winning novel about a teenager who falls silent after being raped; and Ellen Hopkins’ novel about drug addiction, “Crank.” PEN America and the American Library Association have both reported historic surges in bans since the early 2020s, although their methodologies differ. PEN counts books removed even for a short time as a ban, while the ALA only includes books that have been permanently pulled. According to the library association’s most recent report, published in April, some 5,600 instances of bans took place during the previous year. CORRECTION (Oct. 5, 2026, 3:30 p.m. ET): A previous version of this article misstated the name of the author of the book “Sold.” It is Patricia McCormick, not Patrick.

articles.title: Turkiye, Pakistan agree Saudi Arabia military deployment under Mecca pact
articles.summary: The three countries agree to trigger collective deterrence measures in response to ‘heinous attacks’ by Yemen’s Houthis.
articles.body:
The Mecca Alliance says it has agreed to trigger collective deterrence measures in response to “heinous attacks” by Yemen’s Houthi group against Saudi Arabia.

In a statement on Monday, the Pakistani Foreign Ministry said Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye had decided to “provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment” to the kingdom.

Saudi Arabia’s Defence Minister, Khalid bin Salman, said the member countries agreed to trigger the deployment in response “to the attacks and all those responsible for them”.

The announcement comes as the Saudi-backed Yemeni government has launched a counteroffensive to push the Iran-aligned Houthis back from territory captured last month.

The agreement was reached during an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee under the three countries’ Mecca Alliance in Riyadh.

The mutual defence pact was signed in August, shortly before the Houthis launched their offensive in Yemen, which has included attacks against Saudi targets. Questions as to whether Islamabad and Ankara would agree to trigger the agreement have persisted since.

However, with hostilities increasing in Yemen, the committee agreed to “move immediately” to implement the collective defence measures to “ensure their rapid deployment in the Kingdom,” the joint statement reads.

The defence commitments will be executed under “approved arrangements” and the laws of the three countries, the statement added.

The Mecca Defence Alliance emerged as a response to intensifying regional conflicts, including the war by the United States and Israel on Iran.

The agreement to form the new alliance was signed by the three countries on August 7. It declares that an attack on any one of the three states will be treated as an attack on all – mirroring a key NATO stipulation.

While steps to institutionalise the Mecca Alliance followed, the agreement did not initially give details on the military ‌‌or ‌‌defence obligations of each country.

Following a barrage of missiles launched by the Houthis toward Saudi Arabia in early September, Pakistan’s Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said any attack on the kingdom could trigger the agreement.

“If there is unprovoked aggression, or a spillover of whatever is happening in Yemen into Saudi Arabia, definitely the Mecca agreement will become operational,” he told the Pakistani media outlet Geo News.

However, no action has been taken until now, with analysts noting that Pakistan and Turkiye remain keen to continue acting as mediators of the US-Iran conflict.

The three members of the alliance combined have nearly 1.4 million active troops, about 3,400 military aircraft, 6,000 tanks and more than 340 naval assets, according to the 2026 Global Firepower Index.

articles.title: UK ‘threatens to expel 27 Israeli diplomats’ over Jerusalem consulate
articles.summary: Israel ordered East Jerusalem consulate to be closed after Britain sanctioned settlements in the occupied West Bank.
articles.body:
The United Kingdom has threatened to expel 27 Israeli diplomats should Israel proceed with plans to close the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem, according to unverified Israeli media reports.

The Ynet outlet reported on Monday that the British Ambassador to Israel, Simon Walters, had conveyed the warning to Israeli officials. Israel ordered the closure of the consulate by October 8 in retaliation for the British decision to sanction illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank.

According to the report, the British government has threatened to expel one Israeli diplomat for each of the 27 British diplomats whose diplomatic status at the consulate would be terminated in the event that it is shut.

Israel ordered the consulate’s closure after Britain imposed sanctions targeting illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank, including a ban on imports.

The consulate operates separately from the British Embassy in Israel and handles relations with Palestinians in East Jerusalem, the occupied West Bank and Gaza, including political and consular affairs.

Britain’s National Security Adviser, Jonathan Powell, travelled to Israel last week in an undisclosed attempt to persuade Israeli officials to reverse the closure, the Reuters news agency reported on Monday. The talks did not produce an agreement, although discussions are continuing.

The British embassy in Israel has declined to comment on the reported threat, according to Ynet.

articles.title: 2 dead, multiple injured in school bus crash with children on board
articles.summary: Three students were airlifted from the bus to the hospital.
articles.body:
A school bus filled with children rolled over in a multi-vehicle crash Monday morning in central Florida, killing two and injuring multiple others, according to authorities.

The bus was traveling to a high school and carrying 39 passengers, including 37 high schoolers, the bus driver and the driver's 9-year-old daughter, Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd said in a press conference Monday morning.

Two people died in the crash, including a tenth-grade girl on the bus and the driver of a Jeep involved in the crash, Judd said.

Five to seven trauma alerts were issued and multiple people are being treated at the hospital, including one in critical condition, according to Judd.

The crash occurred in Winter Haven, Florida, and was reported at about 6:15 a.m. on Monday, according to authorities.

A preliminary review of video footage shows that the school bus was driving in its lane when a white Chevy Malibu traveling the opposite direction drifted over the center line for unknown reasons, hitting the bus, Judd said. This caused the bus to crash into a silver Jeep head-on, he said.

Another vehicle was involved, bringing the total to four vehicles impacted by the crash, officials said.

"It was a horrible crash," Judd said. "It was a terrible, tragic morning."

Emergency helicopters flew some victims to the hospital, while others left in ambulances or private vehicles, according to the sheriff's office.

Three students from the bus were airlifted to the hospital, 22 students were driven by another bus to the hospital, four students were transported by their families to the hospital, and seven students plus the bus driver and his daughter were taken to the hospital by ambulance, according to Judd.

Most of those who were treated for injuries were released from the hospital Monday, officials said.

High schoolers called their families on their cell phones to notify them of the crash as officials worked after the incident to reunite students with their families, officials said.

Traffic homicide investigators are responding at the scene and will continue to gather information throughout the day.

T he Polk County Sheriff's Office, Winter Haven Fire, Winter Haven Police, Haines City Police, Polk County Fire Rescue and Polk County Public Schools responded to the crash.

All information is preliminary and more details will be released in another press conference expected on Tuesday, according to Judd.

"It's an incredibly tragic event that took place this morning," Fred Heid, Polk County Public Schools superintendent, said at the press conference. "We drill for this with our students intentionally so that they know how to evacuate a bus in the event of an accident, and we are very, very fortunate today that more students were not seriously injured, including the driver."

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

articles.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye activate Mecca defence pact amid Houthi attacks
articles.summary: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have agreed to immediately implement their collective defence commitments and ensure the “rapid deployment” of agreed
articles.body: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have agreed to immediately implement their collective defence commitments and ensure the “rapid deployment” of agreed military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia, following an emergency meeting of the three countries’ Mecca Defence Alliance in Riyadh.The decision was announced in a joint statement shared by Pakistan’s foreign ministry on Monday. The move will be carried out under “approved arrangements” and in accordance with the national laws of the three countries.The three countries had signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in August, under which an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all. The agreement did not specify the military commitments or defence obligations of each country at the time.Alliance moves to strengthen collective responseThe committee overseeing the defence pact decided to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom, according to the joint statement.“The committee decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom … thereby enhancing readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats,” the statement said.The statement also said, “The parties affirmed that the security of each party is an integral part of the collective security of the three countries.”Saudi defence minister Khalid bin Salman said the Strategic Political and Defence Committee of the alliance had “agreed to activate collective deterrence measures” in response to recent attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group.“The committee agreed to activate collective deterrence measures within the framework of the Alliance in response to the attacks and all those responsible for them,” Salman said on X.He added that the committee had expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia over the “heinous attacks” targeting the kingdom and its holy sites.Houthi attacks raise tensionsThe Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said on Thursday that the Iran-aligned group had attacked a power distribution station in Medina that supplies electricity to the Prophet’s Mosque, one of Islam’s holiest sites.The joint statement from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye also condemned what it described as the attempted targeting of Mecca and Medina, and reaffirmed their rejection of attacks or threats against Saudi Arabia’s security and territorial integrity.The developments come amid renewed fighting in Yemen that has spilled into neighbouring Saudi Arabia, with the Houthis launching drone and missile attacks targeting Saudi territory.Saudi-backed forces launch Yemen offensiveSaudi-backed forces have also launched a major offensive against the Houthis in Yemen.According to news agency AP, forces allied with Yemen’s internationally recognised government recaptured the strategic town of Dhubab, just north of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, along with the towns of Bab and Hadeid.The offensive was launched under air cover from the Saudi-led coalition. Saudi coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki said 100 fighter jets were supporting government forces and that the coalition had secured “air protection” of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and destroyed hundreds of Houthi targets.The offensive followed the Houthis’ capture of the town of Turbah on Sunday. The Saudi-backed government said it was mobilising troops across areas under its control, while Presidential Leadership Council head Rashad al-Alimi said the operation was aimed at “recovering the remaining territories” controlled by the Houthis.Al-Alimi later said the operation, dubbed “Yemen Dawn”, had begun with the aim of “restoring state institutions, liberating” Sanaa and ending “the Houthi terrorist militia coup”.Fighting revives Yemen conflictThe latest escalation has revived Yemen’s civil war after a four-year ceasefire. The Houthis captured Sanaa in 2014, forcing the internationally recognised government to flee into exile in Saudi Arabia.The Houthis have made advances along Yemen’s western coast, including the capture of Mokha and several Red Sea islands.These gains enabled the group to control the Yemeni side of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a major maritime chokepoint through which about 12% of global trade transits.US secretary of state Marco Rubio said Saudi Arabia and the United States have a defence agreement and that the Saudi-backed government had a right to defend itself.US officials also said Washington had provided support for the Saudi-led offensive, including intelligence sharing, target identification and planning, AP reported.The latest bout of violence has killed at least 959 people and wounded more than 4,200, according to the World Health Organization, while about 174,097 people have been displaced inside Yemen.More than 3,000 others have fled across the waters to Djibouti, according to the UN migration agency.You use AI every day. articles.title: Two killed, Indian among injured after Russian drone hits Turkish cargo ship
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: At least two people were killed and several crew members, including an Indian national, were injured after a Russian drone strike caused a fire
articles.body: NEW DELHI: At least two people were killed and several crew members, including an Indian national, were injured after a Russian drone strike caused a fire aboard a Turkish-owned civilian cargo vessel in the Black Sea.The Indian Embassy in Romania said three Indian nationals were among the crew of the vessel, identified as MV Royad Mammadov, and that one of them was injured and receiving medical attention.“We have learnt of an attack today on commercial vessel MV ROYAD MAMMADOV in the Black Sea. As per preliminary information, there have been 2 casualties (foreign nationals) while some crew members have been injured and are undergoing medical treatment in Romania. It is further reported that there are three Indian nationals among the crew members,” the embassy said in a post on X.The embassy said it was in close contact with the relevant authorities to establish further details about the safety and welfare of the Indian nationals.Three Indians among crew, all reported safeIndian ambassador to Romania Manoj Mohapatra spoke to the three Indian crew members who were receiving treatment at Constanța County Hospital. The embassy said the hospital's chief physician confirmed that all three were in good health and receiving necessary care.“Amb @manojifs spoke with the three Indian nationals receiving treatment at Constanța County Hospital. He also spoke with the hospital’s Chief Physician, who confirmed that all three are in good health and receiving necessary care. The ambassador assured them of all possible assistance and support,” the mission said.It later said that all three Indian nationals were safe.“We have spoken to them. One of them has been injured and is receiving medical attention. We are in close touch with the hospital authorities. We are extending all possible support for the welfare and wellbeing of the Indian crew members,” the embassy added.The nationalities of the two people killed in the incident were not immediately known.Zelenskyy says captain killed in drone attackUkrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday that two Russian drones had struck a civilian vessel carrying corn in neutral waters.“A horrific strike by two Russian drones on a civilian vessel in neutral waters carrying corn and owned by Turkiye,” Zelenskyy said.He said Azerbaijani and Indian citizens were aboard the vessel and that the ship's captain had been killed. The fate of another person was still being established, he said.“Azerbaijani and Indian citizens were on board. As of now, unfortunately, we know that the ship’s captain was killed. My condolences. The fate of one other person is still being established,” Zelenskyy said.He added that 11 crew members had been rescued, including one who was injured.Zelenskyy said Ukraine had repeatedly proposed concrete measures to de-escalate the conflict and improve security in the Black Sea.“Pressure is needed to restore global food security. And everyone who is genuinely interested in this must help,” he posted.Vessel was headed from Ukraine to ItalyRomania's interior ministry said its Coast Guard was alerted about the fire at around 11 am local time after the vessel was reported in the country's exclusive economic zone, about 30 nautical miles (55 km) south of Sfantul Gheorghe in Tulcea County.The ministry did not confirm what caused the fire. Romanian media reported that the vessel had been hit by a drone southeast of a Black Sea oil platform, but the reports had not been immediately verified by authorities.Romania's Naval Authority identified the vessel as the Royad Mammadov. According to MarineTraffic, it is a general cargo ship flagged to Saint Kitts and Nevis. It had departed Ukraine's port of Izmail and was headed for Italy.Romanian authorities said 11 crew members had been rescued and two deceased people had been found. Injured crew members were airlifted by helicopter for medical treatment.The Black Sea has faced heightened security concerns amid the Russia-Ukraine war, with attacks affecting commercial shipping and port infrastructure.Fresh incident involving Indian nationalsThe incident came a day after a 52-year-old employee of a pharmaceutical warehouse belonging to Indian owners was killed in a Russian strike in Ukraine's Sumy.External affairs minister S Jaishankar said on Sunday that India had moved beyond advocacy and stepped up efforts in recent months to help resolve the Ukraine conflict by engaging with both Kyiv and Moscow.His remarks came days after Russian President Vladimir Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has “good ideas” to find a mutually acceptable solution to the conflict.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Ukraine says Russian drone attack sinks ship in Romanian waters
articles.summary: The latest suspected incursion on NATO’s eastern flank increases fears that the war in Ukraine threatens to spill over.
articles.body:
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has blamed a Russian drone attack for the sinking of a ship in Romania’s section of the Black Sea.

Romania reported that two people were killed and 11 rescued when a grain ship caught fire and sank in its waters on Monday. The Ukrainian president’s claim suggests the incident is the latest in a series of suspected incursions along NATO’s eastern flank, and will fuel concerns that Moscow’s war in Ukraine could spill over.

“A horrific strike by two Russian drones on a civilian vessel in neutral waters carrying corn and owned by Turkiye,” Zelenskyy wrote on social media.

According to the Romanian Ministry of Internal Affairs, the coastguard was alerted at about 11am local time (08:00 GMT) that a fire had broken out on the ship, adding that it was in the country’s “exclusive economic zone”.

The ministry did not identify the cause of the fire.

Azerbaijani and Indian citizens were on board the ship at the time of the attack, it is reported.

Romania is among several NATO members to have reported incursions this year, as Russia and Ukraine have increasingly turned to launches of hundreds of drones and missiles.

In May, a Russian drone hit an apartment building . In June, a stray Ukrainian maritime drone exploded in the Black Sea port of Constanta. In July , Bucharest summoned Russia’s ambassador after air defences intercepted three drones within the span of one week.

Incursions by Russian drones into eastern European airspace are seen by some as a test of NATO and the European Union’s defences and response capabilities.

The Baltic states have also seen drones enter their airspace throughout the war, with airspace violations contributing to the collapse of Latvia’s government in late May after a dispute over how to respond to the incursions.

The incursions have also prompted Poland to bolster its air defence posture after accusing Moscow of violating its airspace in September. Suspected drones were shot down twice in Moldova.

Romania’s Ministry of National Defence said the Romanian Naval Forces had destroyed nine drifting sea mines in the Black Sea since the start of the war.

articles.title: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson's socialist agenda stalls amid homelessness and public safety concerns
articles.summary: Katie Wilson's socialist agenda faces reality as Seattle's mayor backs more police funding and reverses her stance on surveillance cameras amid public safety concerns.
articles.body: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson, a democratic socialist, has run into major roadblocks while trying to enact her agenda in the city as she grapples with public safety concerns and homelessness. Wilson campaigned on adding 1,000 homeless shelter units in each year of her term, despite concerns from some advisors about the feasibility of the goal, according to The Wall Street Journal. However, her administration's current plan calls for adding nearly 1,000 shelter beds by the end of 2027, the Journal reported. The mayor told The Seattle Times in September that her original goal was a way to get people talking about the crisis. The city's business community donated $3 million toward the homelessness effort. Joe Nguyen, president and CEO of the Seattle Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce, said the money wasn't used as City Hall ran into bureaucratic roadblocks. "Welcome to government," he told the Journal in response to the challenges. SEATTLE MAYOR SAYS SOBRIETY WON'T BE REQUIRED AT NEW HOMELESS SHELTER Wilson surprised her supporters with a proposed budget released in September that included no new taxes and more funding for police, the Journal reported. "I have made the difficult decision to transmit a budget without major new revenue," Wilson said in a speech in September, according to KOMO News. "Right now, we don't have good options to raise more progressive revenue that don't also come with great risks. Our economy and especially our downtown are fragile. In that context, raising additional revenue through JumpStart is not the right move." Wilson and the Seattle Police Department faced scrutiny after a shooting at the Bite of Seattle food festival in July left three people dead, including one suspect, and led to the resignation of the police chief, who was out of town at the time of the shooting. The Journal reported, "A communication breakdown between the mayor’s office and Seattle police kept the public in the dark about the shooting for five hours, and the official emergency alert system went unused." The mayor's office did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment. WILL SOCIALISM SAVE SEATTLE? CITY ADVOCATES STRUGGLE TO FIND SOLUTIONS AS HOMELESS, DRUG ADDICTS FLOOD STREETS Psychotherapist Jonathan Alpert, author of "Therapy Nation," told Fox News Digital, "This is a good example of socialism's appeal colliding with the realities of governing." "Socialism is seductive because the promises sound good: more housing, more services, greater fairness, less inequality," he said. "It’s easy to campaign on those ideas. It gets much harder when you’re actually responsible for a budget, public safety and whether the city is functioning." "The result: Wilson is now doing some things that don’t fit so comfortably with the politics she campaigned on: more police, more cameras, spending cuts and fewer big promises," Alpert continued. "Crime has a way of forcing politicians to become practical pretty quickly." "I don’t think this proves that every socialist idea is doomed," he added. "But it does show the gap between promising people what government should do and figuring out what government can actually do. That’s the harsh reality check that more socialists should realize: Ideology is much easier when you don’t have to govern." SOCIALIST MAYOR’S NEW ANSWER TO RAMPANT RETAIL CRIME IGNITES FURY: ‘BANDAGE ON A BULLET WOUND’ Wilson faced backlash on social media in May after a 77-year-old man was seen on video being beaten by two individuals in a crime that was captured by closed-circuit television cameras, a tool that Wilson has denounced in the past as something that makes the community feel unsafe. She also opposed the expansion of Seattle's network of surveillance cameras while on the campaign trail and said it would make the city "more vulnerable" to President Donald Trump's "attacks on immigrants, trans people and big cities in general." Wilson sought to halt a $3 million effort to add more cameras in January, according to the Journal. After two teenagers who attended Rainier Beach High School were shot and killed at a bus stop in Rainer Beach, the mayor moved toward expanding the project, the outlet reported. "When you’re faced with the realities of sitting in the seat and doing the job, you have to deal with those realities," Bob Kettle, a city council member and chair of the public safety committee, told the Journal on why Wilson wasn't governing like a socialist. SEATTLE MAYOR'S INTERVIEW CUT SHORT AS STAFF BLOCKS QUESTIONS ON GUN VIOLENCE, SURVEILLANCE The Journal also reported that Jon Scholes, president and CEO of the Downtown Seattle Association and an advisor to the mayor, joined a group of business leaders on a trip to San Francisco to meet with members of San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie's administration. "They clearly have serious people doing serious work," Scholes said of the trip. "I mean, it’s not just symbolism and performance. It’s real governance and management." articles.title: California Amber Alert teen rescued in Mexico; father accused of incest arrested
articles.summary: The teen’s father was arrested after he was allegedly found in possession of narcotics, the Monterey County sheriff said.
articles.body: A 14-year-old Monterey County, California, girl who was the subject of an Amber Alert has been rescued in Mexico and her father, who is suspected of sexually abusing her, has been arrested, authorities said. The Monterey County Sheriff’s Office said the teen, whom NBC News is not naming because she is a victim of sexual abuse and a minor, was rescued by Mexican law enforcement. Sheriff Tina Nieto said the teen’s father, 38-year-old Sergio Galvez Perez, was arrested after he was allegedly found in possession of narcotics. Galvez Perez is wanted on several felony charges, including incest, lewd or lascivious acts with a child under 14, unlawful sexual intercourse and child endangerment. Nieto said Mexican authorities are aware of Galvez Perez’s pending charges in Monterey County and worked with local police and the FBI to rescue the girl. “[She] is safe and is currently in the care of local authorities in Mexico,” Nieto added. The announcement comes almost a month after the California Highway Patrol issued an Amber Alert for the teen and her father. The alert was issued amid an investigation into the remains of an infant found on Aug. 1 on the side of a road in Monterey County. It’s not clear how the infant died, but investigators said the infant’s body showed signs of traumatic injury. Investigators eventually identified Galvez Perez and the teen as being connected to the newborn, which authorities have named “Baby Angelita.” The sheriff’s office said they believe the 14-year-old conceived the child as a result of her father’s sexual abuse, gave birth on the side of a road and left the baby. While the Monterey County Sheriff’s Office had initially said the teen girl was wanted on suspicion of murder, the District Attorney’s Office said no charging decision had been made. “We recognize that the 14-year-old is a victim of her father’s abuse. No child should ever have to endure such horrific circumstances,” the DA’s office said in part in a statement on Sept. 2. “Our office works with victims of abuse every day and understands that children who have experienced abuse can face extraordinary barriers to safety and may be unable to seek help on their own, particularly when they are under the control or influence of an abuser. The responsibility for getting a child to safety does not rest on the child. Our priority is to ensure that this young girl is safe and has access to the support and services she needs.” The teen’s mother, Ofelia Garcia Ortega, was arrested in August on allegations of child endangerment and later released on bail.

articles.title: Ex-‘American Idol’ contestant Caleb Flynn sentenced to life without parole in wife’s murder
articles.summary: The “American Idol” contestant and music pastor was found guilty last week in the shooting death of his wife in their Ohio home.
articles.body: A former Ohio music pastor and “American Idol” contestant has been sentenced to life without possibility of parole for killing his wife in their Dayton-area home earlier this year. Caleb Flynn, 40, was found guilty of aggravated murder in the February shooting of Ashley Flynn, 37, a schoolteacher and volleyball coach. Flynn and their two daughters were home when police arrived. Before issuing the sentence, Judge Jeannine Pratt said he would be punished because he posed a high risk of harm to the community. “The layers of deceit, manipulation and cruelty are hard to fathom,” Pratt said Monday. “And you used your faith to manipulate the lives of others.” Flynn maintained his innocence Monday, crying and shaking as he read a statement to his family and Ashley’s. “I loved her and loved her. She was my wife. She was beautiful and amazing in countless ways,” Flynn said. “I will continue to fight for my innocence as long as the Lord allows me to, since I did not kill my wife.” To his two children, Flynn apologized and said they are his greatest joy in life. He thanked his parents for their love and kindness and said their support throughout the trial was “supernatural.” “I never knew that love this fierce was possible until the moment that I held you for the first time,” Flynn said to his daughters. “Please know your daddy is so proud of you and loves you beyond what words can describe.” Flynn’s daughters were not in court, but other family members read written statements from the preteen girls who were ages 9 and 11 when their mother was killed. “I love you deeply with all my heart and it’s sad that you can’t love anyone but yourself,” read the letter from his daughter Alissa. In her letter, his daughter Ava said photos and videos of her father on trial online have been inescapable. “My heart aches to see you hurt, but then I think it was your choice,” she wrote. “It was your choice to have that affair.” Both daughters implored their father to confess to murdering their mother. Along with their grandparents, uncle and aunt, who read statements in court, the girls said their faith has been helping them get through their grief. Ashley Flynn’s sister, Kayla Keyt, said during her victim statement that her family could not overcome their sense of shock and despair after learning that Flynn betrayed them in such a violent and horrible way. “We trusted you. We believed in you. We honestly would have laid down our lives for you,” Keyt said. Prosecutors said Flynn’s wife was defenseless in bed when he shot her and then feigned a home invasion to mislead investigators. Flynn frantically called 911 and said someone had broken in while he slept on the couch. He woke up to the sound of gunshots, he told investigators. He said that a day before the killing, a man had come to their home and handed his wife an American flag while making a “weird sales pitch for America.” But Flynn’s lover, Alleigha Botner, testified in court that he talked about hating his wife and having thoughts of killing her. Jurors heard AI-generated love songs that prosecutors say he made for Botner and some of the more than 100,000 text messages that authorities say they exchanged. Miami County Prosecuting Attorney Paul Watkins read a statement to the court and shook his head as prosecutors said he endangered his children’s lives when he killed his wife while they were home. “This case is about deliberate choices, the destruction of an irreplaceable life and the permanent devastation left behind,” he said. “The defendant has never accepted responsibility or expressed genuine remorse for the life he ended,” Watkins added.

articles.title: Former American Idol contestant Caleb Flynn sentenced to life in prison for murdering wife
articles.summary: Caleb Flynn, a former music pastor from Ohio, fatally shot his wife Ashley in February before trying to cover it up.
articles.body:
A US man who once appeared on the TV talent competition American Idol has been sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole for murdering his wife.

Caleb Flynn, 40, was found guilty last week after a short deliberation by the jury, which rejected his claim that an intruder broke into his Ohio home and shot his wife, Ashley Flynn, as she slept.

He was also found guilty of eight additional charges, including aggravated murder and tampering with evidence.

Letters from his two daughters were read in court during the sentencing hearing on Monday, pleading with him to finally admit his guilt and questioning why he killed their mother.

Flynn, a former music pastor, fatally shot his wife, a 37-year-old teacher, in February before staging their home in Tipp City to appear as if someone had broken in through the garage.

Flynn claims he was asleep when he heard gunshots and found his wife dead in bed after finding the garage door open. Their two children, ages 9 and 11, were also sleeping in the house at the time.

His wife's sister, Kayla Keyt, read a victim impact statement saying the murder had caused his daughters to question their Christian faith and had "shattered a family who trusted you".

One of his daughter's letters read: "Dear Daddy, I don't even know where to start. How could you do such a thing?"

She also said: "Mommy was the perfect person... And then you chose to kill the only mother I ever had."

The other daughter's letter began "Dear Caleb", rather than addressing him as her father, and asked him to "tell everyone what you did it and receive your outcome".

"You made me feel like an idiot thinking I could trust you," his daughter said. She added that she continues to have faith in God, and that she will never visit her father in prison.

Flynn sobbed loudly as the letters from his children were read.

The sentencing hearing also included Flynn reading a statement expressing love for his family, apologising for unspecified "decisions" that he made, and again claiming that he did not kill his wife.

"I made vows to Ashley on our wedding day. I failed those vows," he said.

Judge Jeannine Pratt called Flynn an "extreme" risk to the public as she imposed her sentence.

The murder verdict last week followed eight days of testimony, during which several incriminating text messages Flynn sent to his former mistress, Alleigha Botner, were read out and AI-generated songs were played that prosecutors said he made for her.

Evidence presented during trial included police body camera footage and activity on Flynn's iPhone and Apple Watch from around the time of the murder when he claimed to have been sleeping.

The prosecution also called dozens of witnesses, including Botner, whom he met while she was an intern at his church.

Botner read aloud in court some of their 100,000 text messages, including one where Flynn wrote: "I was up until 4am last night crying, literally thinking of ways to kill her and not go to jail."

In another message, he wrote: "I just want her dead and gone."

Flynn did not testify during the trial, and his defence team called no witnesses.

His lawyer, Patrick Mulligan, has said he plans to file a notice of appeal, telling reporters last week: "There's a lack of evidence on prior calculation and design."

Mulligan argued that evidence of infidelity was not evidence of murder and questioned why Flynn was being accused of tampering with evidence because his gun could not be found.

This gun, which had been kept in the console of his truck, has been missing since investigators arrived at the scene and found the truck's centre console open.

Prosecutor Paul Watkins read a statement from Ashley Flynn's family in court after the verdict in September, saying: "Ashley loved Jesus with her whole heart."

"She loved people," the statement continued. "Most of all, she loved being a Mum."

Flynn briefly appeared on American Idol in 2013, saying that he loved his wife "more than anything".

articles.title: SIR row: Will annul Election Commission orders not in keeping with law, says Supreme Court
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday asked the Election Commission, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to clarify whether crucial
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday asked the Election Commission, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to clarify whether crucial decisions regarding the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter rolls were taken unilaterally by the CEC, and said it would injunct (bar) those decisions by the three-member commission which were neither unanimous nor by majority.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said irrespective of powers vested in the CEC, the law clearly mandates that all decisions must either be by unanimity or by majority among the three members of the EC. “If we come across instances (where CEC has unilaterally taken decisions), we will annul them,” it said.The statement came after senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for a PIL petitioner, strongly argued for an interim direction to the EC to only take decisions by unanimity during pendency of the petition as the amended CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, gave the CEC enormous powers.The PIL has sought scrutiny of the validity of SIR decisions and ”alterations” in Form 6 for new voters. Singh said since the court could not undo elections, a direction must be issued that in the interregnum, EC must follow the statutory mandate. He pleaded that EC be directed to preserve all records on SIR decisions and Form 6 alteration and produce them before SC for scrutiny.CEC, ECs need to either rebut or endorse allegations about ‘unilateral decisions’Let us have some authenticated facts before us through their responses. They must respond in a clear and transparent manner. If the records show some of the decisions are not taken by majority, we will injunct those. But we cannot put the cart before the horse, the bench said while also issuing notices to the Centre, deputy EC Manish Garg and EC’s director general (IT) Seema Khanna.This has set the stage for the CEC and, more crucially, the two ECs to either endorse or rebut the allegation that important decisions on SIR were taken by Gyanesh Kumar unilaterally and in violation of the law which lays down that the commission’s calls are to be made either unanimously or, failing that, by majority. The allegation, based on a newspaper report, is at the core of the controversy which has reignited opposition to SIR.Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for a PIL petitioner, also questioned the validity of Section 16 of the 2023 Act, which provided that “no court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings against any person who is, or was, a CEC or an election commissioner for any act, thing or word, committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty or function”.He said this was way beyond the immunity enjoyed even by SC judges and especially when it was not extended even to the PM.Justice Bagchi said, “We will examine the expression ‘or was’. Protection while in office is understandable. Such protection (as provided under Section 16) is perhaps only with regard to the President. It is not given to constitutional court judges under Judges Inquiry Act.”Singh pleaded for suspension of the CEC or divesting him of his authority. When the bench asked who would conduct elections, Singh said the other two ECs would do it. He said in the interim, the SC-mandated selection panel for CEC should be brought back in which the CJI is included along with the PM and the LoP. The 2023 Act replaced the CJI with a Union minister nominated by the PM.When the bench declined, Singh said the situation was so grave that it could undermine the very basis of our democracy. “Today, the CEC is acting in a manner which is contrary to the statute under which he is appointed. Court should pass some interim orders (restraining the CEC from discharging his functions), otherwise the country will burn,” he said.Patna-based petitioner Rakesh Kumar Singh has sought a direction to EC to “produce before SC the complete original and primary records relating to the matters pleaded herein, including minutes, agendas, approvals, file notings, work allocation and delegation orders, IT-access records, server logs, audit trails and database-change histories concerning the functioning of the commission, ERONet/EClNet, alteration of Form 6 and filing of appeals before the Bengal appellate tribunals”.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Bath wheelchair user 'had to crawl' off GWR train from London
articles.summary: Phoebe's mum said watching the incident was "traumatic" and left her feeling "helpless".
articles.body:
A wheelchair user was left in tears as she crawled on her "hands and knees" through a train after being told a ramp could not be used to help her off.

Phoebe Tesoriere, 24, was on a Great Western Railway (GWR) train from London Paddington to Bath Spa with her parents when it happened.

Her family spoke to the assistance desk and was taken to the only designated wheelchair space on the train. Phoebe said she was assured a ramp and assistance would be waiting, but on arrival was told she was in a carriage beyond the platform, leaving her unable to get off.

GWR said it was "really sorry" and admitted "we let her down, both when we helped her board and at several points during her journey".

Phoebe, who has hereditary spastic paraplegia which causes weakness and stiffness in the leg muscles, said: "My mum specifically asked if a ramp and assistance would be waiting at Bath Spa. We were assured it would be."

While on the train, staff checked which station she would be getting off at numerous times during the incident in December 2025, she added.

Despite this, Phoebe was not told the carriage she was directed to would stop beyond the platform, leaving her unable to use a ramp to get off.

Phoebe and her parents had been returning to Bath, where she now lives, after attending a concert in London the night before, which she bought as a gift for her mum and dad before her diagnosis.

When they got to Bath Spa, she said they were told by staff to stay on the train and get off at Bristol Temple Meads - a 15-20 minute journey - before buying another ticket back to Bath Spa so she could get off.

The family explained this was not possible as Phoebe's grandparents were waiting at the station to pick them up and take her back to Caerphilly, where she was living at the time.

Phoebe said she was told by staff to try and get her wheelchair through the train aisle, but it did not fit so she crawled through three carriages.

"I was crying. People were staring," she said.

"One passenger reached down to stroke my back and apologised to me, telling me what was happening wasn't acceptable.

"She was trying to comfort me, but in that moment I felt like a dog."

Phoebe's mum Kirstin Tesoriere said watching the incident was "traumatic" and left her feeling "helpless".

"When I close my eyes I can still see it, the pity on other passengers' faces. It was humiliating for her."

Phoebe said her parents lifted her back into her wheelchair to get off the train using the ramp, but staff were not waiting to assist her.

Phoebe wants to see a big improvement in accessible transport in the UK. She said: "It's ridiculous that disabled passengers are still expected to go through this."

Due to the nature of Phoebe's diagnosis, her condition is expected to get worse over time.

Kirstin said she wanted to "make lovely memories" with her daughter but that the family had not used public transport since the incident.

"She's just scared now and she's already lost so much to her diagnosis," she said.

"You just want your children to be happy."

Phoebe made a formal complaint to GWR on the day it happened, but the investigation was not completed until May.

In its response, the train company admitted Phoebe's experience was "extremely poor" and took accountability for what went wrong.

It confirmed Phoebe would receive compensation but, despite sending her bank details as requested, she has still not received any money and said GWR had "ignored every email I have sent" since June.

"Nearly nine months after I complained, I am still fighting to get an answer. No disabled passenger should ever have to crawl."

Kirstin said she understood "mistakes were made" but believes her daughter has been treated "inexcusably" since then.

"I can't forgive them for how they've made an awful traumatic experience last for months," she added.

In emails seen by BBC Wales, GWR said it had made changes to "how we manage passenger assist for customers travelling from London Paddington" as a result of Phoebe's complaint.

It said: "There were opportunities for us to recognise that there would be an issue at Bath Spa, and we failed to identify them.

"In my view, the situation you were placed in - and your subsequent action to leave the train - was entirely avoidable.

"Put simply, this should not have happened. I am truly sorry for the distressing and uncomfortable experience you had when leaving the service."

In response to BBC Wales, GWR said: "We are really sorry. Ms Tesoriere should have been able to travel with confidence and dignity and we let her down, both when we helped her board and at several points during her journey where we had opportunities to put it right.

"We have apologised to her personally and have made improvements to how we support customers boarding at London Paddington, so no-one else goes through this."

Regarding her compensation, a spokesman added that the company was "doing everything we can to complete the final steps as quickly as possible".

articles.title: Trump says US ready to aid Russia with plague outbreak in Siberia
articles.summary: Russian authorities quarantine hospital, monitor 200 contacts after suspected pneumonic plague death in Siberia.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump says the United States is ready to help Russia with a suspected pneumonic plague outbreak .

“We are looking at it very strongly. We just heard about it,” Trump said, adding that he had not spoken to Russian President Vladimir Putin about it but is prepared to offer US support.

“It’s a disease we used to be able to control,” Trump said. “Even with great advancement, the germs have really become relatively stronger than they were, and things that used to work on pneumonia don’t work anymore … anyone that has that kind of problem, we will help.”

The World Health Organization (WHO) said based on unofficial information it has received, the “public health risk to the general population appears to be low”.

Earlier on Monday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio downplayed the danger as well. “I don’t think it’s cause for alarm, but it is cause for focus and a cause to just keep an eye on it,” Rubio said.

Russian authorities have quarantined a hospital and are tracing the contacts of an employee at a plague research institute in the remote Siberian region of Irkutsk who died of a suspected pneumonic plague infection. Local media identified the employee as 28-year-old laboratory technician Darya Shipilova.

Official details about the incident have been limited, and Russian media reports say authorities in Irkutsk have placed nearly 200 people under medical observation.

On Sunday, Russia’s official TASS news agency reported that the country’s consumer protection agency, Rospotrebnadzor, said an employee at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East was diagnosed with “pneumonia of unknown aetiology” or origin. The agency also said it had expanded sample testing from the patient and found no microorganisms associated with her work.

On Saturday, the governor of neighbouring Buryatia region said in a post on his Telegram channel that a woman in Irkutsk had “died, maybe of the plague”.

In a statement to Al Jazeera, a US State Department official said: “We encourage Russian authorities to share accurate information quickly and openly.”

Pneumonic plague is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, usually found in small mammals and their fleas. According to the WHO, the plague is highly infectious and can be fatal if not treated early.

The plague ⁠comes in three forms affecting different parts of the body. Pneumonic plague, an infection of the lungs, triggers the patient to cough out infectious airborne droplets.

If identified quickly, antibiotics can treat the disease. Left untreated, it can be fatal in one to six days.

articles.title: Chicago woman shot 5 times by CBP officer files federal lawsuit
articles.summary: Attorneys for Marimar Martinez alleged a new analysis of the bullets’ trajectories shows Border Patrol Agent Charles Exum wasn’t in front of her vehicle and the last shot went through the rear passenger seat.
articles.body: A woman who survived being shot five times by a Border Patrol agent in Chicago filed a federal civil lawsuit Monday against the U.S. government as her attorneys allege that new evidence shows the agent was not in danger for his life and should face criminal charges. Marimar Martinez, a teaching aide at a Montessori school, was shot in her car by Customs and Border Protection agent Charles Exum in October. The shooting occurred during the Trump administration’s mass immigration enforcement surge in Chicago last year, known as Operation Midway Blitz. The lawsuit was filed a year after Martinez was shot under the Federal Tort Claims Act, which allows private citizens to sue the federal government. Federal agents cannot be directly sued, the attorneys said. The lawsuit alleges negligence, battery, assault, intentional affliction, emotional distress, false arrests, false imprisonment and malicious prosecution, attorney Michael Gallagher said at a news conference Monday. “The reality is the shoot wasn’t justified. She almost lost her life as a result. She’s been dealing with the physical and mental injuries ever since then,” he said. The attorneys also urged the Justice Department and local prosecutors to file criminal charges against Exum. The Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that consistent with policy, Exum was placed on administrative leave, though it did not immediately say whether Exum is still on leave. DHS referred all other questions to the Justice Department, which declined to comment on ongoing litigation. According to Christopher Parente, also an attorney for Martinez, the investigation and an analysis of the scene his firm commissioned showed that Border Patrol agent Charles Exum shot Martinez without justification and was not in danger at the time of the shooting. The attorneys showed a visual reconstruction alleging where Exum would have been standing as he opened fire on Martinez based on the bullets’ markings in her vehicle, her wounds and surveillance video. Martinez was not driving at Exum when he shot her five times, as he had previously claimed, the attorneys said. One of the bullets, they alleged, went through the side of the rear passenger-side car seat, which showed Exum could not have been standing in front of the car when he shot. “He was in no way, shape or form in the path of the vehicle. She was actually driving away from him, and we established that he charged her,” Gallagher said. Exum was not wearing a body camera at the time of the shooting. In August, DHS said all ICE officers and agents in the field would be required to wear body cameras. Martinez spoke briefly at the news conference, saying, “Right now, we’re just focused on moving forward with the civil case and just heal emotionally and physically.” “I’m just glad to see another year, be with my family,” she said. “I want to spread awareness, because what’s happening is not normal. We shouldn’t stay here and normalize what’s happening.” After the shooting, Martinez and another person at the scene were charged with using their vehicles to attempt to ram federal law enforcement officers, but the charges were dropped after federal prosecutors filed a motion to dismiss their own case. The motion came after additional video of the incident was shown and after it was revealed that Exum had bragged about the shooting in messages to other officers. According to Reuters, records presented at the hearing showed that in a group Signal chat with other agents, Exum wrote: “I fired 5 rounds and she had 7 holes. Put that in your book boys.” In a message to another recipient, Exum sent a news article about the event followed by the message: “Read it. 5 shots, 7 holes,” Reuters reported. Parente asked Exum what he meant by those messages at the time. According to records presented at a hearing, Exum responded: “I’m a firearms instructor and I take pride in my shooting skills.” Martinez’s case has been one of the highest-profile examples of federal authorities accusing civilians of ramming into vehicles driven by immigration agents.

articles.title: LAUREN GREEN: I was Fox News Channel's first on-air hire. Here's how a dream became a powerhouse
articles.summary: From a basement construction zone in New York City to a state-of-the-art newsroom, a founding anchor reflects on Fox News Channel's 30-year rise.
articles.body: A plywood board resting on two sawhorses was the anchor desk. There was a single camera, no prompter, and a small office tucked away from the construction zone. When I think of the early days of Fox News Channel, I remember the pre-launch days when Fox was still a dream and a wish. I was the first on-air person hired for Fox News Channel. My official start date was August 5, 1996, which was nearly two months before the first broadcast. But a few weeks earlier, I came to New York City to look for an apartment with my mother, and we were given a tour of the newsroom on C-1 (aka the basement). It was huge. Down to the studs, it was being transformed into the nerve center of the newest cable news channel. During those first weeks, a ragtag crew of producers and writers and I were tasked with churning out practice newscasts to see how it would feel to do seven minutes of news at the top and bottom of every hour. It was a daunting task, as we were also creating a format and learning what worked and what didn’t. Pretty soon, we moved off-site to a rented studio to have greater access to cameras and equipment before the launch. MARTHA MACCALLUM: AFTER 22 YEARS, HERE'S WHY I'M GRATEFUL TO CALL FOX HOME In the summer of 1996, for those who are old enough to remember, the blockbuster movie "Independence Day" was released. It was a 20th Century Fox product, part of the Fox family. It made more than $100 million during its opening week. And I thought, "Wow! This cable network is bound for success if this is the kind of quality handiwork it puts out." That prediction proved truer than I could have imagined. Today, Fox News is the number one cable news outlet. It is a juggernaut that others are chasing and seeking to emulate, if only in style, if not substance. WATCH: FOX NEWS CELEBRATES 30 YEARS OF HEADLINES, DEBATES, LAUGHS AND MORE Studio space has expanded exponentially as Fox has taken over the entire ground level and several floors of 1211 Avenue of the Americas. The newsroom is a new, state-of-the-art facility on the second floor (the C-1 space is now a company fitness center). CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION I’ve got a new office, which I continually fill to the gills with books about religion and theology. And many of the producers with whom I work today were not born yet or were still in diapers or pre-K when Fox launched in 1996. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Reflecting on 30 years, there’s so much to be thankful for. So much of what looked precarious became a blessing. That’s what life teaches us. I think that during three decades of change, ups and downs, tragedies and triumphs, joys and hopes, there has been one constant in my life: Fox News Channel. And I am forever grateful! articles.title: France braces for national day of student protests after injuries and mass arrests
articles.summary: France prepares for a day of protests in support of students who’ve been demanding more investment in education.
articles.body:
France is braced for major protests on Tuesday, after organisers called for a nationwide day of action in support of students demanding more investment in education.

It comes after a week of demonstrations, which saw students blockading hundreds of schools, at least 190 students injured, and more than 5,000 people arrested.

One student had his hand blown off during a confrontation on Monday, while another was reportedly struck in the head by a tear gas grenade last week.

France's prime minister said the government had announced measures to address their demands, but the Union Syndicale Lycéenne (USL), a major organiser of the protests, said the government had offered "nothing concrete".

The organisation called on people to join their mobilisation on Tuesday in the face of "this political deadlock and what we describe as unprecedented repression of the movement".

Some other organisations have also shown their support for the students, with the teachers' union SNES-FSU urging its members to join Tuesday's protest.

The radical-left La France Insoumise (LFI) party leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon described the protests as the "most powerful high school and university student youth movement" since 1968 - a year of major unrest, which saw millions of workers go on strike.

The wave of demonstrations began in September in Paris and has spread across the country, with students protesting over a range of issues, including overcrowded classrooms, run-down buildings, and a lack of teachers.

The protests were started by high school students, who were later joined by university students.

On Sunday, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced a series of measures to "address the difficulties faced by secondary school students and education staff", promising "visible changes" in schools.

However, he also said: "We will make no concessions to violence. We stand by students and staff who have been assaulted, as well as police officers and gendarmes who have been injured."

The unrest has not only seen schools blockaded, but also rubbish bins set on fire. Education Minister Édouard Geffray said 24 schools had been "burned and ransacked" since the start of the protests.

Violent clashes between students and the police have led to some serious injuries throughout the course of the protests so far.

On Monday, a 15-year-old boy's hand was blown off during a confrontation near a school in the northern city of Lens. The student was transferred to a nearby hospital and his injury is not life-threatening, according to officials.

Last week, Eden, 14, was badly hurt in Saint-Ouen-l'Aumône after reportedly being struck on the head by a tear gas grenade.

The student suffered "a double jaw fracture" and had to undergo "extremely major surgery", according to his lawyer.

Speaking at a news conference on Monday, Eden's mother said her heart was "shattered".

"It's shameful, it's appalling, it's violent, it's horrific," French media outlet BFMTV reported her as saying.

"This should not happen. They are dealing with children who are asking for better conditions in which to study."

Among the 5,060 people arrested since the start of the movement, 87% were minors and 13% were adults, according to France's justice ministry .

Fourteen people have reportedly been placed in pre-trial detention, while 1,802 people are facing prosecution, including 319 adults and 1,483 minors.

The USL has accused police of using excessive force against the protesters. Responding to this allegation last week, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the demonstrations had been policed in "an extremely proportionate manner".

While France's next presidential election is still months away, the protests and the response by French authorities have been heavily politicised.

The government and hard-right politicians have blamed the hard left for fuelling the protests. Lecornu said LFI was being "irresponsible" in calling for the movement to expand.

The leader of the hard-right National Rally, Marine Le Pen, has also criticised the left for its response.

"This is no longer about high school student protests. It is about riots organised by professionals and overseen by deputies from La France Insoumise," she said, calling for a new anti-rioting law to be passed.

Meanwhile Mélenchon, the LFI's party's presidential candidate, has been blaming the police for "abuses of power", calling on people to take to the streets to "protect the youth demonstrations".

The left-wing mayor of Marseille, Benoît Payan, condemned the "unacceptable violence" in his city. While young people were "legitimately concerned" about their future and public services, they must express themselves calmly, he said.

articles.title: Former Wall Street banker spent about €20 million restoring his family’s Irish castle; 25 years later, Castle Freke is still unfinished
articles.summary: More than two decades after Stephen Ralfe Evans-Freke brought Castle Freke back into his family’s ownership, the West Cork estate is still undergoing
articles.body: More than two decades after Stephen Ralfe Evans-Freke brought Castle Freke back into his family’s ownership, the West Cork estate is still undergoing restoration. Evans-Freke, a retired Wall Street investment banker, bought the ancestral property around the turn of the millennium, after the Evans-Freke family had owned it for generations before losing it in 1921. He suggested to The Irish Times in 2025 that he had paid less than €500,000 for the property. The much larger expense has been the restoration itself: he estimated that he had spent between €500,000 and €1 million a year over roughly 20 years, putting the total at €10 million to €20 million. By June 2026, the Irish Examiner reported that Evans-Freke estimated the project had cost about €20 million while Castle Freke remained only partially complete.From family property to a long restoration projectEvans-Freke first knew Castle Freke as a child. The Irish Times reported that he retained a connection to the house throughout his life, including carrying an oil painting of the property with him. Evans-Freke later moved to the United States, where he worked as an investment banker on Wall Street.The Irish Times places his repurchase of Castle Freke around the turn of the millennium, while the Irish Examiner's 2026 account also describes it as a return to family ownership more than 25 years earlier. Restoration began in 2004. Evans-Freke also owns nearby Rathbarry Castle, which has been another base for the family. Rather than following what he described as the conventional approach of putting the entire project into the hands of construction firms, Evans-Freke assembled a smaller team to oversee the work. He assembled a smaller team to oversee the restoration, bringing in specialist tradespeople for the work. Evans-Freke also said an architectural firm had quoted €1.5 million to detail the proposed works.Stonework, chimneys and decorative interiorsThe Irish Times described Castle Freke as a 50,000-square-foot property, with Evans-Freke saying restoration had focused on roughly half of that area. Work has included relining more than 40 chimneys, repairing battlements after their lead was removed in the 1950s and repairing external walls. The interiors have required similarly specialised work. Restoration of the fan-vaulted ceilings in the music room began around 2017, according to The Irish Times. The project has involved specialist stuccodores, including Kevin Holbrook, whose work includes elaborate decorative schemes created specifically for the restored interiors. Both were reported to have been appointed master plasterers of the Worshipful Company of Plasterers, a City of London livery company with a history stretching back about 500 years. The Irish Times also reported that Keogh was the first woman to hold the master plasterer title in the company's history. The decorative programme incorporates references to Evans-Freke and his family's background. A frieze depicts him as a rotund mole holding a martini glass, while the Children of Lir appear above the staircase. Another stucco scene depicts the Lady of the Lake presenting Excalibur, and a separate work shows the Norse god Odin with his wolves, including one named Freke. The Irish Times linked these elements to different aspects of the family's heritage.Why Castle Freke is still unfinishedDespite the years of work, the restoration has not reached completion. The Irish Times reported in June 2025 that utilities still needed to be installed and that parts of the interior, including a bedroom floor and half-basement, remained unfinished. At that time, Evans-Freke estimated that the main block could require another three years once its eventual use had been decided. The Irish Examiner reported a year later that he expected the project to take several more years at a minimum.A hotel is one possibility Evans-Freke has floated for the property. The Irish Times reported that he had carried out a feasibility study into a super-luxury hotel, while the Irish Examiner said he had suggested that a five-star hotel could give West Cork a facility he believes the area needs. The property's final use has not been settled. The restoration's cost has risen far beyond the amount Evans-Freke suggested paying for the property itself. By his own estimate, the work had cost between €10 million and €20 million by 2025, based on annual spending of €500,000 to €1 million over roughly two decades. The Irish Examiner reported in June 2026 that he put the figure at about €20 million. He has also said that he received no grant aid for the restoration.CastleFreke Gin turns the restoration into a second ventureThe restoration has also provided the setting and inspiration for a separate business. Evans-Freke developed CastleFreke Gin after years of experimenting with botanicals and spirits. The Irish Times reported in 2025 that he had begun developing the recipe while recovering from foot surgery about a decade earlier, using the dining table at Rathbarry Castle as a place to experiment. By June 2026, the gin had moved from development to commercial launch. The Irish Examiner reported on June 14 that Evans-Freke had launched CastleFreke Gin in New York the previous weekend. A June 5 announcement from Castle Freke Distillery also confirmed the US debut and said US distribution would begin in July.The Irish Examiner reported at the time that an Irish and European launch was scheduled for the following month. However, the distillery's current website and recent company updates now say availability in Ireland and the UK will follow later in 2026, so a completed Irish launch should not be stated without a more specific confirmation. Castle Freke therefore remains both a restoration project and the centre of a newer family-branded business. More than 25 years after Evans-Freke returned the property to family ownership, substantial work has been carried out on its structure, stonework and interiors, but the building is still not finished and its eventual use remains undecided.You use AI every day. articles.title: Christa Pike execution failure spares murderer who bailed victim out just to kill him
articles.summary: Gary Wayne Sutton's Dec. 3 execution is on hold after Tennessee's botched lethal injection of Christa Pike prompted Gov. Bill Lee to halt deaths.
articles.body: The execution of a double murderer who bailed one of his victims out of jail only for the man to be shot dead — and then killed his sister when she went looking for him — has been put on hold after Tennessee's botched attempt to lethally inject Christa Pike for her role in the "satanic" torture and murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville in 1995. Gov. Bill Lee halted the death penalty across the state for the rest of the year — but there was only one scheduled, the Dec. 3 execution of convicted double murderer Gary Wayne Sutton. His uncle and co-defendant, James Dellinger, died of natural causes on death row in 2023. FORMER KNOXVILLE POLICE CHIEF SAYS INVESTIGATORS ARE STILL HAUNTED BY COLLEEN SLEMMER'S MURDER 31 YEARS LATER Sutton has maintained his innocence — but in separate trials, he was convicted in the murders of Tommy Griffin and Connie Branam, a brother and sister who were killed on Feb. 21 and 22, 1992. articles.title: Only 15% going to work use public transport: NSO
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Long traffic snarls, a common feature on roads across the country, may be linked to how people commute to work.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Long traffic snarls, a common feature on roads across the country, may be linked to how people commute to work. Only 15% of workers use public transport such as buses, trains, trams or auto-rickshaws, while 46% rely on two-wheelers or cars, according to the first-ever National Household Travel Survey (NHTS) by the National Statistics Office (NSO).Two-wheelers account for 43% of workers' commute nationally and cars for 3%. In urban areas, reliance on these vehicles is higher, with 53% of workers using two-wheelers and 5.7% travelling by car.28.3% of people reach workplace on foot: NSOWalking is the second most common mode of work commute in the country, accounting for 28.3% of workers, 10.7% use bicycles. More than a third of rural workers (36%) walk to work, compared with just 14% in urban areas, as per the data. The survey was conducted between July 2025 and June 2026 and included trips which are longer than 1 km. Travelling to and fro has been counted as two trips in the survey.The survey showed a worker takes an average of 25 minutes to reach the workplace. In urban areas, the commute takes 27 minutes, compared with 23 minutes in rural areas. The morning commute remains heavily concentrated before 10 am, with nearly 95% of workers leaving home for work then.In terms of cost, workers spend an average of Rs 785 a month on commuting, with men spending substantially more (Rs 835) than women (Rs 533). The gap widens further in rural areas, where men spend more than twice as much as women — Rs 674 against Rs 307.In contrast, student mobility shows a markedly different pattern. Walking is the single largest mode, accounting for 37% of students travelling to educational institutions, followed by buses at 29.5% and bicycles at 15.8%. Around 88% reach their institutions within 30 minutes, while the average journey takes 23 minutes. Nearly four in five students leave for school between 7 am and 10 am.Besides meeting the railway ministry’s specific data requirements, the survey is expected to provide insights into how, when and why people travel. “Information on travel patterns and public transport use will help identify gaps in existing transport systems, assess accessibility, optimise routes and improve service frequency and scheduling,” said NSO in a statement.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
